steps.what: Name the decision each performance indicator must serve.
Build the indicator from the agreed source fields.
Test the indicator against one known week.
Accept the performance indicator for publication.
Publish the indicator on the operations view.
Say whether the indicator matches the unit decision.

tasks.design: The analyst names the decision. {BI} builds the indicator from {ERP} fields and tests it on a known week. It is published only after the analyst accepts it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Indicators were copied between spreadsheets and nobody could say which decision they served.
tasks.enabler_now: The source fields for on-time, cost and stock already exist.
tasks.still_hard: A green indicator can hide a lane the business unit does not control.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst can refuse an indicator that would punish the wrong unit.

ambition.what: Retire an indicator that no longer matches a decision.

tasks.altitude: Choosing and accepting indicators stays. Rebuilding them by hand does not.

reach.task: Act on an indicator the analyst has published
reach.learn: Which source fields the indicator uses and which it ignores

evidence.claim: Comparing a lane cost with a contracted rate is a table check. A floor walk is not.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from a named decision to a published indicator. The unit lead's comment is other-role time and is not saved. Targets and bonuses are out of scope.
Test the existing {ERP} and {BI} views before any custom extract.
Structured fields are indicator id, source field, unit id and week. The source system produces the measure. Fallback: a field that is empty for the test week blocks publication.
EU data-protection rules apply. A study of named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which business units will accept a shared definition.
research_questions: How often a published indicator is later withdrawn.

already_counted.description: Accepting an indicator after the known-week test

incremental.description: Keep source-field names aligned when the ledger changes

approvals.approved_version: indicator the analyst accepted after the test week

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Stable source fields save the build and the publish. The decision and the acceptance stay. The unit lead's comment is not saved. The low case is a test week with empty fields.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Collect the current steps the procedure must cover.
Draft the operating procedure from the approved notes.

loop.purpose: Draft a procedure from approved process notes.
loop.check: Each step names an owner and a source field.
loop.stop: Stop after one draft or when a step has no source.
loop.why_not_simpler: A blank template cannot see the exception this site hits.

steps.what: Edit the business rules the draft got wrong.
Sign the standard operating procedure.
Publish the signed procedure to the operating file.

tasks.design: Approved process notes feed one draft in {DOCS}. The analyst edits the business rules and signs the procedure. Publication uses that signed version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were rewritten from scratch in mail each time the floor changed.
tasks.enabler_now: A draft can be produced from notes that already name the owner and the field.
tasks.still_hard: A procedure that ignores the exception will be ignored on the floor.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows which rule the site actually follows.
tasks.altitude: Editing and signing the procedure stay. Retyping the standard steps does not.

reach.task: Follow the signed procedure on a shift
reach.learn: Which exceptions are written down and which are not

evidence.claim: Comparing a lane cost with a contracted rate is a table check. A floor walk is not.
A procedure draft still needs a named person to sign it before it is the operating file.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from approved notes to a signed procedure. Bargaining a change with a carrier is out of scope.
Test the existing {ERP} and {BI} views before any custom extract.
Structured fields are step id, owner role, source field and exception flag. The process notes produce them. Fallback: a step with no source is left for the analyst, not invented.
EU data-protection rules apply. A study of named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Who is allowed to sign a procedure that binds a shift.
research_questions: How often the signed procedure is bypassed on the first month.

incremental.description: Review procedures when a source field or a site rule changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Stable notes save the first draft and the publish. Editing and signing stay. The low case is a process whose exceptions are not written down.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Prepare questions for the staff interviews.
Tour the facilities named in the study brief.
Interview key staff about the flow just toured.
Answer the interview from the shift just worked.
Write findings that name the efficiency gap.

tasks.design: The analyst prepares a short question list, then tours the facilities and interviews staff in person. The findings note is written from those notes, not from a floor plan alone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tours were informal and the notes never met the cost file.
tasks.enabler_now: A question list can be prepared from the study brief before anyone walks.
tasks.still_hard: People will not describe a failing step if the note is used against them.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst hears what the layout drawing does not show.
tasks.altitude: The tour and the interview stay. Only the question list is prepared ahead.

reach.task: Host the tour and answer for the shift
reach.learn: Which questions will be asked and what the note will be used for

evidence.claim: Comparing a lane cost with a contracted rate is a table check. A floor walk is not.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from a study brief to a findings note. The supervisor's time in the interview is other-role time and is not saved.
Test the existing {ERP} and {BI} views before any custom extract.
Structured fields are facility id, question id and a gap the analyst names after the tour. Fallback: a gap nobody will state on the record is omitted.
EU data-protection rules apply. A study of named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether staff may be interviewed about their own step times.
research_questions: Which findings the supervisor will confirm in writing.

already_counted.description: Writing findings after the tour and the interview

incremental.description: Keep the question list aligned with the studies still open

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Preparing questions is the only small saving. The tour, the interview and the supervisor's answers stay. Supervisor time is not saved. The low case is a site that will not host the tour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Model an operational or facility issue.

steps.what: State the operational question the model must answer.
Run the logistics model on the stated inputs.
Judge whether the modeling result fits the floor.
Record the recommendation the model may support.
Facilities engineer comments on a layout the model moves.

tasks.design: {BI} runs the model from the question and the lane table. The analyst judges whether the result fits the floor. A facilities engineer comments when the result moves a layout. That comment is not the analyst's time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Models were run and then presented as if the floor had already agreed.
tasks.enabler_now: The lane table can be calculated once the question is stated.
tasks.still_hard: A model that moves a wall still needs someone who owns the building.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst can tell a feasible flow from a picture the site cannot run.
tasks.altitude: Stating the question and judging the fit stay. The model run does not. The engineer's comment is unchanged.

reach.task: Comment when a model result moves a layout
reach.learn: Which constraints the model did not receive

evidence.claim: Comparing a lane cost with a contracted rate is a table check. A floor walk is not.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from a stated question to a model note and an engineer comment. The engineer's time is other-role time and is not saved.
Test the existing {ERP} and {BI} views before any custom extract.
Structured fields are question id, lane id, volume and constraint. The lane table produces the numbers. Fallback: a constraint the model cannot hold is stated in the note, not dropped.
EU data-protection rules apply. A study of named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which facility changes the engineer is willing to comment on.
research_questions: How often the floor rejects a result the model ranked first.

already_counted.description: Judging whether the model fits the floor

incremental.description: Keep model inputs aligned with the lanes still in use

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A stated question with a complete lane table saves the model run. The judgement stays. Engineer time is not saved. The low case is a question the lane table cannot express.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Floor walks, interviews and the choice of which saving is real stay with the analyst. Standard lane costs and indicator refreshes leave the spreadsheet.
reach: Warehouse supervisors, on which floor facts a flow study needs.
Transport planners, on which rate fields a lane comparison needs.
skills_to_grow: Marking a missing rate instead of filling it.
Separating a floor constraint from a model result.
role.ambitious_version: A lane exception arrives with its cost, its floor note and the name of the person who may change the plan.
